title: Generated facts tables: can the question be answered from the facts listed?
decision: whether a question can be answered from the facts of a table under the rules of reading written above it (yes) or at least one fact it needs is not listed (no)

source.name: generator build/gen_answerable_facts.py
source.version: gen_v4, 2026-10-08: founding years drawn from 1880-2024 without a clamp at 2022, level ladder meta.level 1 / 2 / 3 (hops 2 / 3 / 4 on 20 / 40 / 80 rows, 200 items each), 40 % region-inheritance questions on every level; DIFFICULTY = "v1" regenerates the first version

licence: generated by the benchmark's script (no third-party text)
notes: Version v2 (harder than the first version, which is regenerated with DIFFICULTY = "v1"). 600 items = 300 contrast pairs (meta.pair, group): a facts table with a question (yes) and the same table in which one needed row is replaced by another attribute of the same organisation or the same attribute of a look-alike organisation (no); the asked organisation and attribute keep their number of rows (one neutral filler row is changed as well). The first four lines of the state are the rules of reading (closed world, links only where a parent row says so, every figure needs its own row, one fact - the region - is inherited from the parent). Levels (meta.level, 200 items each): 1 = hops 2 on 20 rows, 2 = hops 3 on 40 rows, 3 = hops 4 on 80 rows (hops = rows the question needs, includes a total over the listed subsidiaries and a region taken over from the parent; rows 20 / 40 / 80 = 8 / 14 / 26 organisations of 2 to 4 families, a near-miss row for every needed row). gen_v4 fixes: founding years are drawn from 1880-2024 (a subsidiary 2 to 20 years after its parent) instead of being clamped at 2022, the nine hops x rows cells are replaced by the level ladder, and 40 of the 100 pairs of every level need the region taken over from the parent (rule 4). The metric is item accuracy; the group allows a pair analysis. Everything is invented and every answer is computed twice (specification and a parser of the rendered text). State length 1358 to 4576 characters (median 2398).
